newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker, lagging behind LME.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker, lagging behind LME.

text.p: COMEX copper ended weaker Thursday, the market failing to keep up with LME as stocks on the New York exchange continued to rise, dealers said.
Much of the buying in copper was completed overnight ahead of the COMEX opening, Fred Demler of E D and F Man International said.

"COMEX has been lagging of late," Demler said. "LME stocks are going down and COMEX stocks are going up. While there was some fund based buying in London there was some fund based selling here on COMEX."

The rising stocks, up 1,179 short tons to 44,961 short tons Wednesday, were helping to prolong the June to July contango on COMEX while the cash to three months backwardation on LME has widened some $40 this week to $100 before slipping back Thursday to $87/$92, Demler added.
LME stocks fell 200 tonnes Thursday to 127,325 tonnes.
July COMEX settled 0.45 cent lower at 121.35 cents per lb, traded from a new life-of-contract high at 122.90 to a low of 121.00 cents. Spot June also went out 0.45 cent weaker at 121.10 cents.
Meanwhile striking unionized workers at Inco Ltd's Sudbury, Onatrio operations said Thursday they were digging in for a long strike as talks with the company remained stalled.
The nickel operation produces about 90,000 tonnes of copper a year.
Also at Ok Tedi copper mine in Papua New Guinea, operations have been reduced due to an unusual dry spell that has affected shipping and production, the company said Thursday.
